findings.reason: the plan should extend velocity's batched reader and cache helpers (or lift one shared reader) instead of forking a second copy that adds public surface and can drift from the owner.
findings.text: `_read_blobs` re-implements the batched `git cat-file --batch` blob reader already owned by `reckon/velocity.py:358 _plan_metas`, and `_cache_path`/`_load_cached`/`_store_cached` (reckon/interface_counts.py:503-538) re-implement the revision-keyed cache plumbing in `reckon/velocity.py:542-613`, reaching into velocity only for the cache root

findings.reason: naming the owner lets the author share one predicate rather than pay for §10's drift-guard assertion, which exists only because the predicate was copied.
findings.text: the census owns the counting predicates `definitions`, `call_name`, `literal_strings`, `interfaces`, `token_lines` and `docstring_spans`, and the plan forked them byte-identically into `reckon/interface_counts.py:76-424` and `reckon/clones.py:72-116`, so three copies of one normalisation rule now drift independently

findings.reason: if the census is reachable by path, one package module can own the predicate and the research script (or a vendored copy) import it, which removes both the fork and the §10 parity node it motivates.
findings.text: this module (and `reckon/clones.py:1`) justifies its port by saying a package caller cannot import the census under `docs/`, yet the plan's §10 test loads that exact census by path via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` (tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py:75-90), so the stated reason for the fork is not true

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `reckon/_timestamps.py` (two functions over 91 lines), `reckon/_observations.py:optional_number`, `reckon/_store.py:write_atomically` and `reckon/clones.py` each hide substantial behaviour behind an interface smaller than what they hide.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan re-implements a batched revision-blob reader and cache already owned by `reckon/velocity.py`, and forks the census's counting predicates into two runtime modules, so a shared predicate now has three drifting copies.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1475, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; the sections that add surface (§4, §5) each name what they retire or why nothing can be (comments c-20261005T0930-s4 / -s5), §2 and §3 name their mass retirements, and §10 adds no definition.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan grounds its counts in the crew-pattern-review code-depth census (§1) and extends the existing `reckon/_store.py` envelope writer rather than adding a parallel store (§3), so it cites what it searched.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — `reckon/interface_counts.py` and `reckon/clones.py` are thin ports over the census whose stated justification ("a package caller cannot import from `docs/`") is contradicted by the plan's own §10 test, which imports that census by path.
